cases.name: specific/enabled-beats-an-enabled-default
cases.note: the channel's own rule is more specific than a workspace-wide one, whatever the store order

cases.name: specific/disabled-is-silence-even-with-an-enabled-default
cases.note: THE clause: a disabled channel-specific rule is the channel's off switch and does not fall through

cases.name: default/answers-a-channel-with-no-rule-of-its-own
cases.note: an empty filter_chat_ids is the workspace-wide default

cases.name: default/disabled-alone-is-silence
cases.note: no specific rule and the default is off, so nothing answers

cases.name: specific/two-for-one-channel-take-the-earlier-created_at
cases.note: rules arrive oldest first, so the tie is the first of them

cases.name: specific/a-disabled-one-is-not-walked-past-to-a-later-specific-one
cases.note: the off switch wins the tie too: the earlier rule owns the channel and it is off

cases.name: default/two-take-the-earlier-created_at
cases.note: same tie-break as the specific rules

cases.name: default/a-disabled-one-is-skipped-for-an-enabled-one
cases.note: unlike a specific rule, a disabled default is not an off switch — it is simply not a default

cases.name: specific/a-rule-for-another-channel-is-neither-specific-nor-a-default
cases.note: a non-empty filter_chat_ids that does not name this channel never answers for it

cases.name: specific/one-rule-may-name-several-channels
cases.note: membership, not equality — the same rule owns every channel it lists

cases.name: specific/exact-string-compare
cases.note: a channel id is compared byte for byte, as Telegram's chat ids are

cases.name: no-rules/is-silence
cases.note: an integration with no rules answers nothing at all
